Smoothed weight of evidence (SWOE) for categorical predictors

Source: R/swoe.r
ks_swoe.Rd

Encodes each level of a categorical variable with a smoothed log-odds of the response, relative to the overall response rate. Useful as a numeric replacement for a factor when screening logistic-type models.

Usage

ks_swoe(data, par, resp, quoted = FALSE, prior.n = 24)

Arguments

data

A data.frame (or tibble).

par

Name of the predictor column (factor or coercible to grouping variable). With quoted = FALSE, pass the column name unquoted (ks_swoe(dt, sex, yn)).

resp

Name of the binary response column (0/1 or logical). Unquoted unless quoted = TRUE.

quoted

If FALSE (default), par and resp are captured with substitute and converted to column names. If TRUE, par and resp must be character strings.

prior.n

Pseudo-count (prior strength) for the empirical-Bayes-style smoothing in the logit; the original implementation used 24.

Value

A numeric vector of length nrow(data) (unnamed), giving the SWOE score for each row's level of par.

Details

Let \(\rho\) be the overall mean of the response and, for each level \(k\) of par, let \(e_k\) be the number of events (response = 1) and \(n_k\) the number of non-missing responses. The smoothed logit for level \(k\) is $$\log \frac{e_k + \rho \cdot m}{n_k - e_k + (1-\rho)\cdot m}$$ with \(m = \)prior.n. A global logit \(\log(\rho/(1-\rho))\) is appended internally for completeness; row values are taken by matching each row's par level to the named level logits.

If \(\rho \in \{0,1\}\), the global logit is undefined; the function clamps \(\rho\) to \((\varepsilon, 1-\varepsilon)\) for that term only, with a warning.

References

The construction follows common “weight of evidence” encodings with Dirichlet-style smoothing; the choice prior.n = 24 matches the historical default in this package.

See also

glm for logistic regression

Examples

set.seed(1234)
dt <- data.frame(
  yn  = rbinom(50, 1, 0.3),
  sex = factor(rbinom(50, 1, 0.55), levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("F", "M"))
)
ks_swoe(dt, sex, yn)
#>  [1] -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#>  [8] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [15] -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347
#> [22] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [29] -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [36] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417
#> [43] -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [50] -1.199417
ks_swoe(dt, par = "sex", resp = "yn", quoted = TRUE)
#>  [1] -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#>  [8] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [15] -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347
#> [22] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [29] -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [36] -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.199417 -1.516347 -1.199417
#> [43] -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347 -1.516347
#> [50] -1.199417
